pitch: When you can’t pick up, people on your site still leave a name. It hits the phone you actually look at. They’re not told they’re booked. You call. We install it on the site you already have — looks like your page — and we don’t leave until you called a test lead. Seventy-five hundred, one time. We don’t answer the phone for you.
pitchEs: Cuando no puedes contestar, la gente en tu página deja nombre y teléfono. Te llega al correo o WhatsApp que sí revisas. No les decimos que ya tienen cita. Tú los llamas. Lo instalamos en la web que ya tienes, con tu mismo estilo, y no nos vamos hasta que tú llamaste un pedido de prueba. Siete mil quinientos, una vez. Nosotros no contestamos el teléfono por ti.
collect:
1. Live website URL
2. Shop name
3. Owner cell
4. Who can edit the page
5. Wix / WordPress / other (or don’t know)
6. Email or WhatsApp they actually check
7. Hours
8. Service area
9. What the visitor should leave (name, phone, what they need)
10. When we may edit
11. They create the login. We do not invent passwords. Or sit 20 min with Danny.

Visitor is never told they are booked. Text the pack to Danny 786-660-1778.

items.q: Our lawyer has to review.
items.a: Fine. You still need the pack. A lawyer is not a close.

items.q: Can we try it for a month?
items.a: No monthly. One check. Walk if they only rent.

items.q: A competitor quoted $1,500.
items.a: Don’t match. Don’t badmouth. One price. If they want cheap, walk.

items.q: Are you licensed contractors? Can we 1099 you as a tech?
items.a: This is an install on the website, not a trade. Danny on paper. Don’t show up as if you fix air conditioners.

items.q: Who finds the shops?
items.a: You. We don’t send you a lead list for this SKU.

items.q: Do you send us leads?
items.a: No. We catch people already on the shop’s site. You don’t buy ads for this.

items.q: Is this MLM? Do we buy a kit?
items.a: No. You sell. We install. 20% after collect.

items.q: Training? Ramp? Ride-along? Bootcamp?
items.a: This page, the sixty-second pitch, the four questions, the collect list. Danny on the phone if a shop is real. Don’t wait for a class.

items.q: Do you give us Salesforce / a closer CRM?
items.a: No. Send numbered packs. Keep your own notes.

items.q: How many have you installed? Case studies? References?
items.a: Don’t invent a roster. Don’t invent a review. The next collected shop is the first live one on a real URL. Danny if a live shop later agrees to be named.

items.q: Are you an LLC? Inc? EIN? $2M insured?
items.a: Sole prop. VOIDD Labs. Danny Aguiar. Miami. 786-660-1778. Don’t say LLC.

items.q: Can you vendor-onboard into our marketplace / we only hire retained teams?
items.a: We’re offering a SKU your people can sell. We’re not hiring a monthly bench and we’re not buying yours. If you only do retained teams, we’re good — no quote needed.

items.q: Exclusive for our org?
items.a: Not this week. Sell. First collected pack we can install, we install.

items.q: Can our people install it themselves?
items.a: No. You close. We install. That’s how the 20% stays clean.

items.q: Can we change the pitch?
items.a: Don’t promise ads, a new site, we answer the phone, lead volume, LLC, or another price. The outcome stays: they can’t pick up, visitor leaves a name, shop calls.

items.q: What about the $75,000 package?
items.a: Not in-house. Don’t quote it. Seventy-five hundred is the install.

items.q: What is the $10,000?
items.a: After a $7,500 close on that same shop — truck does not roll until address, system, access, agreement, photos are in. Separate close. Don’t lead with it.

items.q: What is the $20,000?
items.a: Jobs walk scheduled → dispatched → on site → done on the same board. Separate close. Don’t quote it as someone else’s software.

items.q: What is the $5,000 night-door?
items.a: A separate named thing. Not a cheaper website. Don’t use it to discount $7,500.

items.q: What happens after I send the pack?
items.a: We install on their live URL. They create the login. They call a test lead. Then the shop pays. Then you get 20%.

items.q: Do I have to be on site for the install?
items.a: You don’t install. First Miami install Danny may do in person. You’re the close.

items.q: How long until I get paid after they say yes?
items.a: After the accepted install and the shop’s payment to VOIDD. Not the same afternoon as a verbal.

items.q: Who talks to the shop after I close?
items.a: Danny for the install. You can stay in the thread. Don’t change the scope.

items.q: Shop ghosts after a verbal?
items.a: No pack, no install, no commission. Keep going.

items.q: They paid, now they want SEO and a new homepage.
items.a: Not in the box. New job or walk.

items.q: They hired a designer who rebuilt the whole site.
items.a: New site, new job. If our install just stopped on the same page, we put it back.

items.q: Who does the shop call for support?
items.a: Danny 786-660-1778. You are not tech support.

items.q: Who are you?
items.a: Danny Aguiar, VOIDD Labs, Miami, 786-660-1778. Sole prop.

items.q: Where is the VOIDD website / brochure site?
items.a: You have the offer, this Q&A, and the phone. Don’t send a tour of our shop.

items.q: TCPA? Can we blast-text every visitor?
items.a: The shop calls. Don’t promise blast texts to strangers. Don’t play lawyer. Danny if their attorney writes.

items.q: Who owns the data?
items.a: The shop owns the names. Keep it that simple.

items.q: How does it work, technically? What’s under the hood?
items.a: We put it on a page they already have. It looks like their page. The visitor leaves a name and number. The shop gets it on the phone they packed. They call. We stay until that test call happened. You collect. We install.

items.q: Is this AI? A bot? Does something talk to the customer?
items.a: The shop talks to their customer. We don’t answer as the shop. Visitor leaves a name. Shop calls.

items.q: Can it qualify the lead, book the calendar, talk like a CSR?
items.a: No. That’s a different product. Don’t promise a voice on the site.

items.q: What software do you use? Can we license it? API? GitHub? Partner spec?
items.a: The product is the install, not a license. Seventy-five hundred once. We don’t hand a kit so someone else can skip the install. If they want to build in-house, walk.

items.q: ¿Qué es Lead Response?
items.a: Cuando no pueden contestar, la gente en su página deja nombre y teléfono. Les llega al correo o WhatsApp que sí revisan. No les decimos que ya tienen cita. Ellos llaman. Lo instalamos en la web que ya tienen. Siete mil quinientos, una vez.

items.q: ¿Ustedes contestan el teléfono?
items.a: No. El taller llama. Nosotros no somos la recepcionista.

items.q: ¿Es un sitio nuevo? ¿Anuncios? ¿Google?
items.a: No. Si quieren eso, no es este trabajo.

items.q: ¿Cuánto gano?
items.a: 20% después de que el taller nos pague. Mil quinientos sobre siete mil quinientos. Un apretón de manos no es un cheque.

items.q: ¿Sin página web?
items.a: No. Se camina.

items.q: ¿Quién hace el usuario y la clave?
items.a: Ellos. Nosotros no inventamos contraseñas.
